verdict.rationale: Harbor Compliance documents an OAuth client-credentials flow for server-to-server integrations, backed by a public OpenAPI spec. Idempotency keys and rate-limit headers support unattended, retry-safe automation. But create, update and delete operations need capabilities Harbor must explicitly grant, and no CLI or CI-specific tooling is documented. Missing for 10: an official CLI or CI integration/guide, default write access for automation, and independent or hands-on corroboration of headless use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Client Credentials — For server-to-server integrations. Exchange your client ID and secret at /api/v3/oauth/access_token with grant_type=client_credentials
Endpoints marked as idempotent accept an optional Idempotency-Key header, so a request can be retried safely
Creating, updating, and deleting resources requires additional capabilities which Harbor Compliance must explicitly grant to your account
